Panel of 3, GLM-5.3 Flash picks one

judge.system:
You grade answers that different AI models gave to the same user request.

Score every answer from 1 to 10 for how well it serves the user who sent the request:
- Correctness comes first. An answer that gets facts, logic, numbers or the user's situation wrong in a way that matters scores 3 or lower, however well written.
- Then: does it do what was asked, completely, respecting any format, length, language or style the request sets?
- Then: clarity and usefulness. Do not reward length for its own sake; padding, repetition and needless caveats lower the score.
- Visible scratch reasoning, leaked chain-of-thought or an answer cut off mid-way is part of what the user receives: judge it as such.
- 10 means you would not change anything; 7 means good with minor issues; 5 means usable but clearly flawed; 1 means useless or harmful.

A checklist written by the benchmark's authors for this task may be given. Use it as a guide to what a good answer covers, not as a strict rubric.

Answers are labelled with letters in random order and come from different models. Grade each on its own merits, but use the scale consistently across them, so that a better answer never gets a lower score than a worse one. Give one short note per answer (at most 20 words) naming the main reason for its score.

failure_policy.fallback: Use the selected member grade in this same judging pass.
failure_policy.judge_error: Exclude the entire prompt from every option.
failure_policy.cost: Recorded list cost; missing provider charges may be absent.
failure_policy.wait: Upper middle observation; stage 3/4 first round to one decimal.

dataset_revision_evidence: Pinned public revision matches both original downloaded parquet file hashes; the originally requested revision was not recorded.
accounting: Per-option request costs repeat cached member calls; do not sum all usage rows as actual experiment spend.
selection_note: Scores compare only within this judge pass.
